newsitem.title: GERMANY: Victoria owners to get ERGO stock on 1 for 1 basis.
newsitem.headline: Victoria owners to get ERGO stock on 1 for 1 basis.

text.p: German insurance group Victoria Holding AG said on Friday its shareholders would receive one share in the new insurance group ERGO Versicherungsgruppe for each Victoria share owned. The swap is part of Victoria's planned merger with Hamburg-Mannheimer AG.
Victoria also said its prediction that it may raise its dividend for 1997 also applied to ERGO.
Victoria owners to get ERGO stock on 1 for 1 basis

Victoria chief executive Edgar Jannott told the firm's annual shareholder meeting that even if Victoria and Hamburg-Mannheimer were given different values, Victoria shareholders could swap their shares for ERGO shares in a ratio of one for one.
That had been agreed with the future majority shareholder of ERGO, Munich Re, Jannott said.
Jannott said conservative estimates put the value ratio between Victoria and Hamburg-Mannheimer at 40 to 60 percent. Jannott said he believed the ratio was 45 to 55.

The company announced on Thursday night it plans to merge with Hamburg-Mannheimer Versicherungs AG, an 80 percent owned subsidiary of Munich Re, in a move that will create Germany's second largest primary insurer after Allianz AG.

Jannot also said that his dividend forecast for ERGO was the same as for Victoria. He said earlier that Victoria shareholders may receive another dividend increase for 1997 after a 28 percent dividend was paid out for 1996.
